title: Canonical closed constant exchange and its underived comparison square
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and let $h:X'\to X$ be any scheme morphism. Put $Z'=X'\times_XZ$, with immersions $i',j'$ and projection $g:Z'\to Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Use small representatives of the small etale and pro-etale sites, constant ring sheaves $A_T$, and ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $P_{T,W}=i_*A_W$ for the supported constant module of a closed pair $(T,W)$, $\rho_{T,W}:A_T\to P_{T,W}$ for constant restriction, and $\epsilon_{T,W}:j_!A_{T\setminus W}\to A_T$ for the open adjunction counit [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero].

Consider any of the following inverse images $L$: $h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$, $h_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}$, or $\nu_X^{-1}$ for $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $(P,\rho,\epsilon)$ and $(P',\rho',\epsilon')$ denote its source and target pair, and $q:LA_X\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\mathrm{target}}$ the constant-unit identification. Each $L$ is exact. On both sites $\rho$ is a cokernel of $\epsilon$. The canonical open extension-by-zero comparison carries $L\epsilon$ to $\epsilon'$, using $q$ and the corresponding identification on $U$. The canonical closed exchange $d:LP\to P'$ (the adjunction-mate exchange of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange], respectively its pro-etale or site-comparison analogue) is an isomorphism, uniquely characterized by
$$d\circ L\rho=\rho'\circ q.$$
In particular this characterization specifies the actual canonical exchange, not only the existence of some isomorphism between its endpoints.

Let $\lambda_M:\Gamma_Z(X,M)\to\Gamma_{Z'}(X',LM)$ be the transformation obtained by restricting the inverse-image section map to the kernels of restriction to the complementary opens [def-pur-support-cohomology]; for $L=\nu_X^{-1}$ use the same closed pair in both topologies. These transformations are defined for every module sheaf $M$. Under the coherent inverse-image comparison $k:\nu_{X'}^{-1}h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}h_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}\nu_X^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], put $c_e=h_{\mathrm{et}}$'s closed exchange, $c_p=h_{\mathrm{proet}}$'s exchange and $\gamma_X,\gamma_{X'}$ the site exchanges. Then
$$\gamma_{X'}\circ\nu_{X'}^{-1}(c_e)=c_p\circ h_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}(\gamma_X)\circ k_{P_{X,Z}}.$$
The two composites of the section transformations $\lambda$ around this same square also agree after applying $k_M$ on the target supported sections. These assertions impose no quasi-compactness on $U$ and no finiteness on $h$ or $X'$.

source.place: Tag 03S6, lemma-shriek-base-change (adjunction normalization), and Tag 095L, lemma-ses-associated-to-open (etale constant cokernel); Milne LEC Section 9, Theorem 9.4 functoriality. Pro-etale constant presentation and comparison-square normalization are the agent-formulated refinement of original item steps 1–3 and 9, using the existing pro-etale presentation node, not an arbitrary-sheaf localization theorem.

proof.text: Work in the fixed larger coefficient universe, so the chosen sites are small. The etale and pro-etale inverse-image adjunctions and the comparison geometric morphism are those of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For the etale scheme inverse image, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] explicitly gives exactness and the constant-unit map. Apply [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] to the pro-etale and comparison geometric morphisms and $\Lambda=A$. It supplies exact inverse image on ordinary modules, the canonical $q:LA_X\simeq A_{\mathrm{target}}$ preserving every constant scalar, and compatibility of the underlying units with composition and localization. Thus the same assertion applies on the complementary opens and on the closed schemes. The constant identifications for two successive inverse images are their composite: both carry every constant scalar to itself. This also holds across the specified inverse-image comparison, since constant sheaves are sheafifications of the constant presheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and their constant sections determine maps out of them.

source.place: Tags 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi (2), (5), (6), and 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf; fixed-ring specialization and constant sections

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] with $F=A_X$ on the etale site. Under $i^{-1}A_X\simeq A_Z$ and $j^{-1}A_X\simeq A_U$ its maps are exactly $\rho$ and $\epsilon$. Apply [lem-pur-proetale-supported-constant-presentation] on the pro-etale site. Consequently in every source and target pair $\rho$ is the cokernel of $\epsilon$. The latter cited statement expressly permits a non-quasi-compact open complement. We use its assertion only for the constant sheaf, not for arbitrary pro-etale sheaves.

source.place: Tag 095L, lemma-ses-associated-to-open; pro-etale constant-coefficient version is the existing presentation lemma, modeled on Milne LEC Section 9, proof of Theorem 9.4, p. 67

proof.text: Write $L_U$ for the inverse image on the open and $a:L_Uj^{-1}\simeq j'^{-1}L$ for the localization comparison. The isomorphisms $b:Lj_!\simeq j'_!L_U$ are supplied respectively by [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change], [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] and [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. Here the inverse of the canonical comparison is the open-adjunction transpose of $a_{j_!F}\,L_U(\eta^j_F):L_UF\to j'^{-1}Lj_!F$. For the site comparison this normalization is explicitly [lem-sf-open-comparison-unit-normalization]; the same mate description for scheme pullback follows by composing the open adjunctions and the sectionwise localization identity of [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism]. Use the adjunctions of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] and [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Transposing $q\,L\epsilon\,b^{-1}$ under $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ gives $j'^{-1}(q)\,a_{A_X}\,L_U(j^{-1}\epsilon\,\eta^j_{A_U})=q_U$, by the triangle identity and the constant identifications. Transposing $\epsilon'j'_!q_U$ also gives $q_U$. Hence $q\,L\epsilon=\epsilon'j'_!q_U\,b$: this is the asserted compatibility with the actual counit.

proof.text: Check the normalization of the actual closed exchange before using the cokernel. Put $r=i^{-1}$, $r'=i'^{-1}$, let $L_Z$ be inverse image on the closed schemes, and write $t:r'L\simeq L_Zr$ for the canonical comparison. Let $q_i:rA_X\simeq A_Z$ and $q_{i'}:r'A_{\mathrm{target}}\simeq A_{Z'}$. By [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] and the mate formula [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], $d:Li_*A_Z\to i'_*A_{Z'}$ has transpose $q_Z\,L_Z(\varepsilon^i_{A_Z})\,t_{i_*A_Z}$. Constant restriction $\rho$ is the adjunct of $q_i$, so $\varepsilon^i_{A_Z}\,r\rho=q_i$. Naturality of $t$ now says that the transpose of $dL\rho$ is $q_Z\,L_Zq_i\,t_{A_X}$. The transpose of $\rho'q$ is $q_{i'}\,r'q$. These are equal by the constant-unit coherence from step 1. The adjunction bijection therefore gives $dL\rho=\rho'q$. This calculation uses only adjunction naturality and the triangle identity; it applies unchanged to the pro-etale and site-comparison mates.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change, definition as the adjunct of inverse image of the counit; explicit constant-unit triangle calculation

proof.text: By exactness, $L\rho$ is a cokernel of $L\epsilon$. Step 3 identifies $L\epsilon$ with $\epsilon'$ through isomorphisms on its source and target, so the cokernel universal property gives a unique $\bar d:LP\to P'$ with $\bar dL\rho=\rho'q$. Applying the same property with $q^{-1}$ gives $e:P'\to LP$ with $e\rho'=L\rho q^{-1}$. Then $(e\bar d)L\rho=L\rho$ and $(\bar de)\rho'=\rho'$. Cokernel uniqueness gives $e\bar d=1$ and $\bar de=1$. Step 4 identifies $d=\bar d$. This proves both invertibility and the characterization of the prescribed exchange, not merely an isomorphism of the objects.

source.place: Tags 095L and 03S6; elementary cokernel universal-property argument from steps 1–4

proof.text: Put $N=\nu_X^{-1}$, $N'=\nu_{X'}^{-1}$, $H=h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$ and $H_p=h_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}$. Use the natural coherent comparison $k:N'H\simeq H_pN$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Precompose the two claimed closed-exchange composites with $N'H\rho$. For $\gamma_{X'}N'(c_e)$, step 4 gives $\rho'_{\mathrm{proet}}q_{N'}N'(q_H)$. For $c_pH_p(\gamma_X)k_P$, naturality gives $k_PN'H\rho=H_pN\rho\,k_{A_X}$; step 4 then gives $\rho'_{\mathrm{proet}}q_{H_p}H_p(q_N)k_{A_X}$. The two coefficient maps are equal, since they are the coherent constant identification from step 1. Finally $N'H\rho$ is epic, as a cokernel carried through two exact functors. Cancel it to obtain exactly $\gamma_{X'}N'(c_e)=c_pH_p(\gamma_X)k_P$.

source.place: Tags 00YV and 0H7J; elementary cancellation using the canonical comparison of lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback and steps 1, 4–5

proof.text: For any $M$, let $\sigma_L(M):M(X)\to(LM)(X_{\mathrm{target}})$ be the adjunction-unit section map. The localized direct-image identity in [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] identifies the restrictions of the unit on $X$ and on $U$. In particular $\operatorname{res}_{U'}\sigma_L(M)=\sigma_{L_U}(j^{-1}M)\operatorname{res}_U$, after the canonical open inverse-image identification. Thus a section restricting to zero on $U$ has image restricting to zero on $U'$. Restrict $\sigma_L(M)$ to these kernels to define $\lambda_M$. Naturality of the unit in $M$ gives naturality of $\lambda$. By [def-pur-support-cohomology] these kernels are precisely $\Gamma_Z$ and $\Gamma_{Z'}$ in both topologies. This construction works for every ordinary module sheaf, independently of any higher cohomology.

source.place: Tag 04J0, lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites; Milne LEC Section 9, kernel-of-restriction definition and functoriality

proof.text: For completeness check the units underlying the section square. The right adjoints of $N'H$ and $H_pN$ agree sectionwise: on an etale object $V\to X$ both evaluate a pro-etale sheaf on $V\times_XX'$, with the same restrictions and scalar action. This is immediate from the direct-image definitions [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] and [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Form their composite units by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. The canonical conjugate comparison is $k$; the unit equation in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] says that applying $k_M$ after the first composite section map gives the second composite section map. More explicitly, for $s\in M(X)$ it gives $\Gamma(k_M)(\sigma_{N'}(HM)(\sigma_H(M)(s)))=\sigma_{H_p}(NM)(\sigma_N(M)(s))$. By step 7 each intermediate section has the required support whenever $s$ does. Restricting this equality to the kernels proves the asserted square for $\lambda$. The calculation also identifies the coefficient maps used in step 6 as the actual unit-preserving ones. None of steps 1–8 used quasi-compactness of $U$, or a finiteness condition on $h$ or $X'$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q14-6784f47d1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all eight steps in full against the statements of every cited node and against Stacks 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change) and 095L (lemma-ses-associated-to-open). The item's statement is unchanged from live (unsplit); only the split fields changed. There are no new nodes, the closure check finds no cycle, and the item is neither on the dropped list nor already split live. No SGA source is cited. The 12 declared tool_uses are all generic sheaf or adjunction operations; I accept them. Step 1 gets the exact inverse images and the scalar-preserving constant identification q from prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact and lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image. Step 2: rho is the cokernel of epsilon in both topologies, by the open/closed sequence with Lambda=A and by the pro-etale constant presentation, which needs no quasi-compactness. In step 3 I redid the transpose and it holds: q Lε = ε' j'_!(q_U) b; step 5 needs only an isomorphism b satisfying this equation. In step 4 I checked the mate types; the triangle identity gives ε^i r(ρ)=q_i, so dLρ=ρ'q. Step 5 is a correct two-sided inverse argument through the cokernel's universal property, and it also gives uniqueness. Step 6 is correct cancellation by the epimorphism N'Hρ, with the two coefficient maps equal because both send the section 1 to 1. Step 7 builds λ from the unit section maps and the localization identity. Step 8 proves the section square from the conjugate-isomorphism unit equation. One advisory point: the fact that k is the adjoint conjugate is stated only in the proof and in the Lean of lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback, not in its statement. This is the DAG's fixed reading of that canonical map, spelled out verbatim in lem-pur-comparison-pullback-open-unit, so I do not count it as a C3 fault. Edge cases checked: Z empty, Z=X, h the identity, X' empty, non-quasi-compact U, and arbitrary M. No fixes written.
